prompt.context: The interviewer opens with a personal anecdote: 'I have an odd hobby (odd because this interviewer was male) of knitting. I knit about 10 sweaters per year. I am looking into this as a business opportunity.'
prompt.question: Estimate the size of the hand knitting yarn market in the U.S. (high-quality yarn sold for hobby-type knitting). A second unrelated estimation question is also asked: How many people fly in and out of LaGuardia airport every day?

clarifying_info.q: Should I include yarn used for commercially produced hand-knitted sweaters sold in stores?
clarifying_info.a: No. Most hand-knit sweaters sold in stores are produced abroad and the yarn is produced abroad. Focus on high-quality hand knitting yarn sold in the U.S. for hobby-type knitting.

clarifying_info.q: Can I estimate the number of people who knit, or the number of stores selling yarn?
clarifying_info.a: Good. There are 3,000 specialty stores that sell knitting yarn. Also some bigger stores like Wal-Mart sell a small selection of lower quality yarn.

clarifying_info.q: Can I sample a few stores to estimate typical revenues?
clarifying_info.a: Yes. I have data on 3 stores: (1) Rhode Island store – $100,000 annual revenues; (2) Austin, Texas store in the owner's garage – $40,000 revenues; (3) Massachusetts store – $170,000 revenues.

clarifying_info.q: What is the markup on knitting supplies?
clarifying_info.a: The mark-up on knitting supplies is about 100%, although with sale items it averages around 60%. Variable costs make up about 50% of total expenses.

clarifying_info.q: What is minimum wage (when estimating worker salaries)?
clarifying_info.a: (Interviewer prompts candidate to reconsider a $30,000 salary estimate, implying minimum-wage workers earn closer to $15,000 per year.)

framework: Define scope: high-quality hobby yarn sold in U.S. specialty stores (exclude commercial/foreign production and big-box lower-quality yarn)
Approach 1 – demand side: estimate number of hobby knitters × yarn spend per year
Approach 2 – supply side: estimate number of specialty stores × average revenue per store (chosen approach)
Validate with a break-even / cost build-up to anchor 'average store revenue'
Cross-check: acknowledge sources of over- and under-estimation; adjust toward true market size

questions.prompt: Part 1 – Estimate the U.S. hand knitting yarn market size using a store-based approach.
questions.guidance: Candidate should anchor store-level revenue using a break-even cost build-up rather than relying solely on the three unrepresentative data points. Key expenses: rent (~$500/month), labor (a few workers at ~$15,000/year each), advertising (~$2,000/year). Fixed/variable split: variable costs = 50% of total expenses, implying total expenses = 2× fixed costs. Revenue at break-even = total expenses (at 60% average markup, but interviewer simplifies to just use break-even). Final step: multiply by 3,000 stores. Candidate should then note why the estimate is understated (stores earn profit; Wal-Mart-type sales excluded) and overstated (some revenue is from needles, patterns, accessories, not yarn alone).

math.setup: Build up break-even expenses for an average specialty knitting store, then scale to 3,000 stores.
steps: Fixed (variable) costs: Rent = $500/month × 12 = $6,000/year; Labor = 2 workers × $15,000 = $30,000/year; Advertising = $2,000/year; Total variable costs = $38,000/year
Variable costs = 50% of total expenses → Total expenses = $38,000 / 0.50 = $76,000/year per store
At break-even, revenue ≈ expenses = $76,000 per store
math.answer: ~$228 million (actual market is ~$350 million; gap explained by profit margin, Wal-Mart sales, and non-yarn supplies in the revenue base)

questions.prompt: Part 2 – How many people fly in and out of LaGuardia airport every day?
questions.guidance: Approach via runway capacity, not airline/route enumeration (which is intractable). Break the day into peak, mid-peak, and off-peak windows. Assume planes are spaced apart on runways for safety. Apply a capacity utilization factor per time band. Use an average plane size (~200 passengers). Multiply flights per hour × average passengers × hours per band × number of runways. Bonus credit for noting weekday vs. weekend differences (peak times shift).

math.setup: Model LaGuardia as a runway-capacity problem with time-of-day demand variation. Assume 2 runways.
steps: Define time bands: Peak = 7am–10am and 3pm–8pm (8 hrs total); Mid-peak = 10am–3pm (5 hrs); Off-peak = 8pm–11pm (3 hrs); No overnight flights assumed
Plane spacing: Peak = 5 min apart → 12 planes/hr; Mid-peak = 10 min → 6 planes/hr; Off-peak = 15 min → 4 planes/hr
Capacity utilization: Peak = 100% (200 pax/plane); Mid-peak = 75% (150 pax/plane); Off-peak = 50% (100 pax/plane)
Single runway passengers: Peak = 200 × 12 × 8 = 19,200; Mid-peak = 150 × 6 × 5 = 4,500; Off-peak = 100 × 4 × 3 = 1,200; Total one runway = 24,900
math.answer: ~50,000 people fly in and out of LaGuardia per day

brainstorming.prompt: Why might your $228 million estimate differ from the actual ~$350 million market size?

categories.name: Sources of understatement
ideas: Assumed break-even; real stores earn a profit, so revenues exceed costs
Excluded Wal-Mart and big-box stores that sell lower-quality yarn
Sample of 3 stores skewed toward smaller/garage operations; average revenue may be higher

categories.name: Sources of overstatement
ideas: Store revenue includes non-yarn items (needles, patterns, accessories), not only yarn
Some specialty stores may stock other crafts alongside knitting

recommendation: The U.S. hand knitting yarn market is approximately $228–350 million, centered around $300 million as a reasonable mid-point estimate
The market is larger than intuition suggests for a 'hobby' category, driven by 3,000 specialty stores plus big-box distribution
risks: Estimate is sensitive to assumed number of workers and rent; a store with 3–4 employees doubles the labor line
Wal-Mart/big-box share is unquantified and could be material
next_steps: Validate average store revenue with a larger sample or industry association data (e.g., Craft Yarn Council)
Estimate the big-box segment separately to close the gap to the $350 million actual figure
If pursuing as a business opportunity, assess whether the market is growing or declining (knitting as a hobby trend)
